transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-17
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42m
Attendees: Ava M., Rahul S., Jordan L. — OrbitalCare: Maya T., Ethan C., Priya R., Liam O.

Summary (auto): quick triage of this week's latency/throughput bench vs OrbitalCare's incumbent; spotted p99 tail on longer sequences and transient CPU throttling on the proxy; agreed next steps to run sustained dedicated-slot and share annotated logs.

Topics: 1) bench delta vs IncumbentVendorX baseline 2) routing & batching knobs 3) dedicated-slot request 4) security docs and data residency check

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Ava M.: ok hey everyone, thanks for joining, we have 42 minutes, quick agenda — run through the numbers, triage the p99 tail, and decide dedicated-slot next steps.
[00:18] Maya T.: yeah thanks, excited to see results. we did the evening runs like you asked — two traffic profiles, bursty chat and steady api.
[00:34] Rahul S.: great, i'll share my screen in a sec — the spreadsheet link is in the calendar note, but key headline: median token latency is about 12% better than IncumbentVendorX on the same prompt mix, throughput at 95% load is roughly parity, p99 is where we see the delta.
[00:52] Priya R.: when you say parity — is that per-GPU or aggregated? we need per-request p50/p95 mapped to our autoscaler.
[01:07] Rahul S.: good call, that's an aggregate cluster-level number — per-GPU the throughput is a little higher on our side because of the continuous batching and lower kernel overhead. per-request p99 though spikes for some long-decode cases.
[01:30] Ethan C.: we noticed a couple of timeouts on our end at the 30 minute mark during the steady-run, thought that might be our proxy.
[01:40] Jordan L.: yeah there was one point where the proxy CPU hit 85%, and the K-V cache warmup coincided — sometimes the transcription shows K-V cash which is funny — but basically cache miss storm.
[01:58] Maya T.: K-V cash, ha — ok noted. is the cache warming strategy adjustable on your side?
[02:11] Rahul S.: yes we can tune prefix caching and warm-up thresholds; we also suggested a KV prewarm script in the notes. it's in the bench doc under 'warmup strategy'.
[02:26] Priya R.: we ran two prompt families: short FAQ interactions ~150 tokens and long summarizations ~1,200 tokens. p99 for the long ones was about 1.9s worse vs baseline, which for our SLAs is borderline.
[02:41] Ava M.: got it. any chance that the longer token sequences are hitting a different kernel path causing mem-copy overhead?
[02:52] Rahul S.: possibly — our runtime switches to a different attention kernel past 512 tokens, and if the sequence distribution wasn't expected we can force quantized attention or adjust the chunking to smooth it.
[03:11] Liam O.: quick Q — how reproducible are those p99 spikes? are they deterministic with the same payload?
[03:20] Rahul S.: some are deterministic, some correlate with other traffic bursts. we saw a couple that lined up with heavy embedding requests on the same pool, those bumped context switch rates.
[03:36] Maya T.: embedding requests — we didn't think embeddings would share the same pool — is that our config?
[03:43] Ethan C.: yeah we had endpoints collocated to save cost, maybe that was a mistake.
[03:49] Ava M.: that's a common pattern, we can split embeddings to a separate pool or use routing rules so embeddings hit cheaper slots and generation hits low-latency slots.
[04:05] Priya R.: splitting sounds good, but does that increase cold-start risk?
[04:12] Jordan L.: there is a cold-start tradeoff, you pay a little more for pinned instances, but you can set a small warm pool and use autoscaler to keep baseline. we'll include numbers in the doc.
[04:29] [04:29] (short crosstalk) Maya T.: okay, can you show the heatmap?
[04:34] Rahul S.: sure, — sharing screen — here's the latency heatmap, x-axis is request size, y-axis is sequence length, the red bands at >800 tokens show p99 outliers.
[04:48] Priya R.: looks like the outliers align with a memory reallocation event, see that vertical line at 14:08 in the logs?
[04:59] Rahul S.: yes, that was when one of the nodes triggered ephemeral GC on the runtime, likely due to a concurrent large batch; we pushed a lower batching cap overnight which smoothed it.
[05:16] Ethan C.: can you remind us the batching cap change? numbers?
[05:21] Rahul S.: we reduced max batch size from 64 to 48 for sequences >512, and also enabled aggressive KV caching for prefixes under 256. median dropped 8% across the long-run.
[05:36] Maya T.: and unit cost? did that bump costs?
[05:40] Ava M.: small bump, about 4% on token unit cost in the test spreadsheet — tradeoff is lower p99 and fewer timeouts.
[05:49] Priya R.: for our finance team we need to see cost per 1M tokens at 95th percentile — can you add that to the sheet?
[05:58] Ava M.: yes will add.
[06:02] Liam O.: what's the dedicated-slot request look like? we're considering a dedicated pool for production pilot.
[06:09] Rahul S.: recommended dedicated-slot config: 4x A100-ish equiv slots for steady low-latency flow plus 2 burst slots. we'll map expected QPS and show cost delta vs shared.
[06:23] Maya T.: timeline — we ideally want pilot in the first week of Aug — is that realistic?
[06:29] Ava M.: yes if we lock in dedicated-slot request this week and you confirm VPC peering, we can do a staged handoff.
[06:37] Ethan C.: VPC peering — security had one question about egress rules and KMS access patterns.
[06:45] Jordan L.: we'll send the security pack with the KMS flow diagram; note that for private deployments we can integrate your bring-your-own-KMS via the HSM connector — doc link in the notes.
[06:58] Maya T.: please send; also we need ISO attestation excerpts.
[07:04] Ava M.: will include SOC2 and ISO snippets.
[07:09] [07:09] (brief silence)
[07:12] Priya R.: on routing — you mentioned smart routing and fallbacks, can you explain how that would behave under degraded nodes?
[07:21] Rahul S.: sure — policy can be latency-first or cost-first. under degraded nodes we can automatically route to a compatible quantized variant with higher latency but lower cost, or failover to a regional replica. we can tune thresholds, e.g. if p95 > 600ms, route to fallback.
[07:40] Liam O.: quantized variant — quality delta?
[07:44] Rahul S.: in our evals for this model family quality only dropped marginally in ROUGE/QA tests — we'll attach eval summary.
[07:55] Maya T.: i want to see the quality evals for the exact prompts we have, that will determine if fallback is acceptable.
[08:02] Ava M.: we can run a prompt-level eval in the next 72h if you share canonical prompts.
[08:10] Priya R.: sending those tonight.
[08:13] [08:13] (typing sounds)
[08:16] Rahul S.: quick note on the p99 tail: two-pronged approach — 1) dedicated-slot run to remove noisy neighbors 2) runtime tuning (batch caps and prewarm). both give improvements but the dedicated slot is the more deterministic fix.
[08:33] Ethan C.: what's the expected p99 after dedicated?
[08:37] Rahul S.: our estimate is p99 for long sequences should be within 300ms of median seen in our smaller tests, essentially closing the gap to within 5-7% of baseline.
[08:50] Maya T.: sounds reasonable. can you provide the cost delta with an option to reserve for a month vs on-demand?
[08:58] Ava M.: yes we'll provide monthly reserved pricing and an on-demand comparison.
[09:04] Liam O.: any blocker from our side to start the dedicated-slot?
[09:08] Ethan C.: only VPC peering scheduling and security review.
[09:12] Ava M.: perfect — action items captured.
[09:15] Priya R.: another small item — in the steady-run we saw intermittent 503s that correlate with our own autoscaler making rapid scale-downs. could be config on our side.
[09:27] Rahul S.: yes, scaling oscillation can create short-lived capacity gaps; recommend smoothing policy or min-instance floor.
[09:36] Priya R.: we'll try a 10-minute stabilization window and report back.
[09:41] Maya T.: ok.
[09:44] [09:44] (crosstalk briefly)
[09:47] Ava M.: last thing — documentation artifacts: benchmark spreadsheet (link above), security pack, and a short runbook. we'll also provide a suggested routing policy for your infra team.
[10:00] Maya T.: great, two favors: annotate the sheet with which rows correspond to the 'long summarizations' and include raw p99 logs for the contested runs.
[10:12] Ava M.: yep we'll annotate and upload raw logs to the link.
[10:17] Liam O.: once we have that, finance will sign off on the dedicated slot trial.
[10:21] Ava M.: good. wrap up — recap of next steps?
[10:25] Rahul S.: run dedicated-slot sustained test week of 2026-07-27 (needs confirmation), share annotated sheet and raw logs by 2026-07-20, customer to share canonical prompts by 2026-07-19, customer to confirm VPC peering timing by 2026-07-21.
[10:45] Maya T.: thanks all.
[10:48] Ava M.: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.
[10:52] (call ends)
